references.text: The same law applies to the thank offering: it must be eaten on the day of sacrifice and on the next day; anything left over until the third day must be burned with fire.
It warns that if anyone eats from the thank offering meat on the third day, it will not be accepted and is considered unclean.
Reiterates the principle that sacrificial meat must be eaten on the same day and not left until the next morning.
The Passover lamb was to be eaten that night, and anything left over until morning had to be burned with fire.
The consecration offering: whatever remained of the meat and bread until morning was to be burned with fire.
